what: Strait of Hormuz remains a fault line as Iran and US drift back into war

clean_source_blocks.text: Control of the waterway has become a key point of contention between the US and Iran, as a ceasefire deal falters.

The idea of a hotline emerged from the talks in Switzerland and reflects growing concern that misunderstandings or overreactions by Tehran could threaten commercial shipping through the narrow waterway, which carries roughly a fifth of the world’s oil supply. A military-to-military communication channel between the two fierce enemies is unprecedented, representing a potentially historic breakthrough after decades of hostility between Washington and Tehran. Iran’s state-run Press TV described it as a way to “prevent incidents in the Strait of Hormuz that might lead to military confrontation” in a report on Friday. It will come in handy for two reasons: military deconfliction and avoiding clashes once the US and coalition forces begin demining the strait, insiders say. First, it will give Iranian officials a direct avenue to raise complaints ---

The fragile "no war, no peace" situation since the US and Iran signed a tentative deal last month now seems to have tipped into war. This on-again off-again truce could again wobble back into life through the efforts of increasingly exasperated Arab and Pakistani mediators, and the preference of both sides to avoid a return to a drawn out, all-out war. But its biggest fault line is the status of the strategic Strait of Hormuz - and Iran is again making it clear that its control over this vital maritime corridor is a big, bright red line that neither military, economic nor diplomatic pressure can break. "We told you: keep your word or pay the price," is how Iran's lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf recently phrased it on social media, quoting the agreement.

See more of our coverage in your search results. WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is establishing a direct military hotline with Iran aimed at preventing more dangerous confrontations in the Strait of Hormuz as international forces prepare a major effort to clear mines from one of the world’s most critical shipping lanes. The proposed communication channel between US Central Command and Tehran is a key result of Sunday’s US-Iran negotiations and would allow the two to quickly deconflict military activity and head off incidents that could spiral into a broader conflict. Vice President JD Vance described the arrangement as Iran sending “somebody from the IRGC to go hang out in Doha with somebody from CENTCOM” in a Thursday report by UnHerd. “That’s how we’re going to settle a lot of these disputes,” he added.

Tehran has found backing for that word in the very vague details of the deal - known as a memorandum of understanding - which was drafted in haste in June.

It has been understood differently by both sides from the start.

The US reads that as saying Tehran has to open this strategic strait to the free flow of global oil and gas supplies, along with other vital commodities, including ingredients to produce fertiliser.

WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is establishing a direct military hotline with Iran aimed at preventing more dangerous confrontations in the Strait of Hormuz as international forces prepare a major effort to clear mines from one of the world’s most critical shipping lanes.

The proposed communication channel between US Central Command and Tehran is a key result of Sunday’s US-Iran negotiations and would allow the two to quickly deconflict military activity and head off incidents that could spiral into a broader conflict.

Vice President JD Vance described the arrangement as Iran sending “somebody from the IRGC to go hang out in Doha with somebody from CENTCOM” in a Thursday report by UnHerd.

“That’s how we’re going to settle a lot of these disputes,” he added.

On Friday, after the US military attacked Iran in retaliation for Tehran striking a cargo ship, Vance warned Iran to use the phone in the future.

“Iran signed a ceasefire agreement. We have honored it. If they have disagreements about how the MOU is being applied, they can pick up the phone,” Vance said on X.  “But violence will be met with violence.”

IRGC spokesman Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi went a step further, describing Vance’s claim as “an outright lie,” according to the IRGC-affiliated Fars News Agency.

Iran’s state-run Press TV described it as a way to “prevent incidents in the Strait of Hormuz that might lead to military confrontation” in a report on Friday.

payload.title: Hormuzinsalmi kiristää Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin välejä aselevon horjuessa
payload.summary: Strategisen Hormuzinsalmen hallinta on noussut Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin kiistan ytimeen. Suoraa sotilasyhteyttä valmistellaan vaarallisten yhteenottojen ehkäisemiseksi.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin välinen jännite on jälleen kärjistynyt, kun osapuolten alustava aselepo horjuu ja kiista Hormuzinsalmesta jatkuu. Samalla maat valmistelevat suoraa sotilaallista yhteyttä, jonka tarkoituksena on ehkäistä väärinkäsityksiä ja estää yksittäisten välikohtausten laajeneminen avoimeksi konfliktiksi.

## Strateginen merireitti kiistan ytimessä

Kapea Hormuzinsalmi on yksi maailman tärkeimmistä merikuljetusreiteistä, sillä sen kautta kulkee noin viidennes maailman öljytoimituksista. Häiriöt salmen liikenteessä voisivat siksi vaikuttaa laajasti kansainvälisiin energiamarkkinoihin ja kaupalliseen merenkulkuun.

BBC:n mukaan Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin viime kuussa solmiman alustavan sopimuksen jälkeinen hauras välitila näyttää kallistuneen takaisin sodaksi. Iran pitää asemaansa Hormuzinsalmella keskeisenä rajana, josta se ei ole valmis luopumaan sotilaallisen, taloudellisen tai diplomaattisen painostuksen vuoksi. Iranin pääneuvottelija Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on viitannut sopimuksen ehtojen noudattamiseen ja varoittanut vastapuolta seurauksista, jos lupauksia ei pidetä.

## Sotilaslinjalla pyritään estämään yhteenotot

New York Postin mukaan Yhdysvaltain hallinto on perustamassa suoraa yhteyttä maan asevoimien keskusjohto CENTCOMin ja Teheranin välille. Neuvotteluissa esiin nousseen järjestelyn on määrä helpottaa sotilaallisten toimien yhteensovittamista ja tarjota nopea kanava tilanteisiin, joissa väärinkäsitys tai ylireagointi voisi vaarantaa kaupallisen liikenteen.

Yhteyden tarve korostuu, kun Yhdysvallat ja sen liittolaiset valmistautuvat raivaamaan miinoja salmesta. Raivaustöiden aikana eri osapuolten joukkojen toiminta samalla alueella voisi kasvattaa tahattoman yhteenoton riskiä. Iranin valtiollinen Press TV on kuvannut kanavaa keinoksi estää Hormuzinsalmen välikohtauksia johtamasta sotilaalliseen yhteenottoon.

Suora sotilaiden välinen yhteys olisi poikkeuksellinen askel vuosikymmeniä vihamielisissä väleissä olleille maille. Aselevon palautumista voivat edelleen edistää arabimaiden ja Pakistanin välittäjät, ja molempien osapuolten kerrotaan pyrkivän välttämään pitkää, täysimittaista sotaa. Hormuzinsalmen asemasta ei kuitenkaan ole löytynyt ratkaisua, joten juuri merireitti pysyy neuvottelujen ja mahdollisen uuden kärjistymisen keskipisteenä.
summary_bullets: Hormuzinsalmen hallinta on noussut Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin kiistan keskeiseksi kysymykseksi.
Maat valmistelevat suoraa sotilasyhteyttä vaarallisten väärinkäsitysten ja yhteenottojen ehkäisemiseksi.
Yhdysvallat ja sen liittolaiset valmistautuvat raivaamaan miinoja strategisesti tärkeältä merireitiltä.

Control of the waterway has become a key point of contention between the US and Iran, as a ceasefire deal falters.

The idea of a hotline emerged from the talks in Switzerland and reflects growing concern that misunderstandings or overreactions by Tehran could threaten commercial shipping through the narrow waterway, which carries roughly a fifth of the world’s oil supply. A military-to-military communication channel between the two fierce enemies is unprecedented, representing a potentially historic breakthrough after decades of hostility between Washington and Tehran. Iran’s state-run Press TV described it as a way to “prevent incidents in the Strait of Hormuz that might lead to military confrontation” in a report on Friday. It will come in handy for two reasons: military deconfliction and avoiding clashes once the US and coalition forces begin demining the strait, insiders say. First, it will give Iranian officials a direct avenue to raise complaints ---

The fragile "no war, no peace" situation since the US and Iran signed a tentative deal last month now seems to have tipped into war. This on-again off-again truce could again wobble back into life through the efforts of increasingly exasperated Arab and Pakistani mediators, and the preference of both sides to avoid a return to a drawn out, all-out war. But its biggest fault line is the status of the strategic Strait of Hormuz - and Iran is again making it clear that its control over this vital maritime corridor is a big, bright red line that neither military, economic nor diplomatic pressure can break. "We told you: keep your word or pay the price," is how Iran's lead negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf recently phrased it on social media, quoting the agreement.

See more of our coverage in your search results. WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is establishing a direct military hotline with Iran aimed at preventing more dangerous confrontations in the Strait of Hormuz as international forces prepare a major effort to clear mines from one of the world’s most critical shipping lanes. The proposed communication channel between US Central Command and Tehran is a key result of Sunday’s US-Iran negotiations and would allow the two to quickly deconflict military activity and head off incidents that could spiral into a broader conflict. Vice President JD Vance described the arrangement as Iran sending “somebody from the IRGC to go hang out in Doha with somebody from CENTCOM” in a Thursday report by UnHerd. “That’s how we’re going to settle a lot of these disputes,” he added.
